claims.text: Low hardness in equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi simple solid solutions is governed by grain-boundary character and distribution.
Low strength in equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi simple solid solutions is governed by grain-boundary character and distribution.
Grain boundaries control dislocation movement in this alloy.
Grain boundaries control deformation-twin formation in this alloy.
Controlled variation of grain-boundary character and distribution is the proposed intervention.

A higher fraction of low-angle boundaries combined with a more uniform grain-boundary-character distribution will produce higher hardness than a higher fraction of high-angle boundaries with a more random distribution.

A higher fraction of low-angle boundaries combined with a more uniform grain-boundary-character distribution will produce higher strength than a higher fraction of high-angle boundaries with a more random distribution.
The proposed baseline is an as-cast or annealed alloy having a random grain-boundary-character distribution.
The hypothesis applies to equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi in a simple solid-solution state.
The proposed grain-size applicability range is 1–100 μm.
The proposed tests are conducted at room temperature.
The proposed strain-rate range is 10^-3 to 10^-1 s^-1.
The experiment will measure grain-boundary character and distribution, hardness, strength, and deformation behavior.
The hypothesis is falsified if varying grain-boundary character and distribution produces no significant change in hardness and strength.
